<laravel-boost-guidelines>
Laravel application; follow existing conventions and sibling-file structure. Packages: laravel/framework (LARAVEL) v12, laravel/prompts (PROMPTS) v0, laravel/mcp (MCP) v0, laravel/pint (PINT) v1, laravel/sail (SAIL) v1, phpunit/phpunit (PHPUNIT) v11. Use descriptive variable/method names and reuse existing components. Stick to existing directory structure - don't create new base folders without approval. Do not change the application's dependencies without approval. Do not create verification scripts or tinker when tests cover that functionality and prove it works. You must only create documentation files if explicitly requested by the user. Be concise.

If frontend changes are not visible, ask the user to run `bun run build`, `bun run dev`, or `composer run dev`. If an `Illuminate\Foundation\ViteException: Unable to locate file in Vite manifest` error occurs, run `bun run build` or ask the user to run `bun run dev` or `composer run dev`.

Use Laravel Boost MCP tools. Use `list-artisan-commands` when checking Artisan parameters. Use `get-absolute-url` whenever sharing a project URL. Use `tinker` to execute PHP for debugging or querying Eloquent models directly. Use `database-query` for read-only database access. Use `browser-logs` for browser logs/errors/exceptions; ignore old logs. Use `search-docs` before any other approach and before code changes; use version-specific documentation, broad topic queries, multiple queries, and no package names in queries.

Always use curly braces for control structures, even if it has one line. Use PHP 8 constructor property promotion in `__construct()`. Do not allow empty `__construct()` methods with zero parameters. Always use explicit return type declarations for methods and functions. Use appropriate PHP type hints for method parameters. Prefer PHPDoc blocks over comments. Never use comments within the code itself unless there is something _very_ complex going on. Add useful array shape type definitions for arrays when appropriate. Enum keys are typically TitleCase.

=== laravel/core rules ===
Use `php artisan make:` commands to create new files (i.e. migrations, controllers, models, etc.). If you're creating a generic PHP class, use `php artisan make:class`. Pass `--no-interaction` to all Artisan commands to ensure they work without user input. You should also pass the correct `--options` to ensure correct behavior. Use typed Eloquent relationships; prefer relationships and models over raw queries, joins, or `DB::`; prefer `Model::query()`. Prevent N+1 queries with eager loading; use the query builder for very complex operations. For new models, create useful factories and seeders and ask whether more are needed, using `list-artisan-commands` to check available `php artisan make:model` options. APIs default to Eloquent API Resources and versioning unless existing routes do otherwise. Always create Form Request classes for validation rather than inline validation in controllers; include rules and custom error messages; inspect sibling requests for array/string conventions. Use `ShouldQueue` jobs for time-consuming operations. Use Laravel authentication/authorization (gates, policies, Sanctum, etc.). Prefer named routes and `route()`. Use environment variables only in configuration files - never use the `env()` function directly outside of config files. Always use `config('app.name')`, not `env('APP_NAME')`. Use factories and existing custom states for test models. Follow existing Faker convention (`$this->faker` or `fake()`).

Use Laravel 11's streamlined structure: No middleware files in `app/Http/Middleware/`; `bootstrap/app.php` registers middleware, exceptions, and routing; `bootstrap/providers.php` contains application service providers; **No app\Console\Kernel.php** - use `bootstrap/app.php` or `routes/console.php` for console configuration; commands in `app/Console/Commands/` auto-register. When modifying a column, the migration must include all previously defined attributes. Eager loading may use `$query->latest()->limit(10);`. Prefer a model `casts()` method when consistent with existing models. Use `search-docs` for version-specific documentation.

=== pint/core rules ===
You must run `vendor/bin/pint --dirty` before finalizing changes to ensure your code matches the project's expected style. Do not run `vendor/bin/pint --test`, simply run `vendor/bin/pint` to fix any formatting issues.

=== phpunit/core rules ===
This application uses PHPUnit; all tests must be PHPUnit classes. Use `php artisan make:test --phpunit {name}` to create a new test. If you see a test using "Pest", convert it to PHPUnit. Every time a test has been updated, run that singular test. Tests must cover happy, failure, and weird paths. You must not remove any tests or test files from the tests directory without approval. Run the minimal number of tests, using an appropriate filter, before finalizing. When feature tests pass, ask whether to run the entire suite. Commands: `php artisan test`; `php artisan test tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php`; `php artisan test --filter=testName`.

=== tailwindcss/core rules ===
Use Tailwind CSS classes and existing conventions. Offer to extract repeated patterns into project-convention components. Consider class placement/order/priority/defaults; remove redundancy and group logically. When listing items, use gap utilities for spacing, don't use margins. Existing dark-mode pages/components require matching dark mode, typically `dark:`. Always use Tailwind CSS v4 - do not use deprecated utilities. `corePlugins` is not supported in Tailwind v4. Tailwind v4 is CSS-first using the `<REDACTED_USER>` directive; no separate `tailwind.config.js` file is needed. Import Tailwind
